name: Looking back pose
blurb: A glance over the shoulder: body turned away, face back toward the viewer
title: Looking Back Pose Reference: Over-the-Shoulder Glance & Turn
description: Looking back pose reference: the over-the-shoulder glance, how the neck and spine twist when drawing it, and how to pose and time it in photography.
answer: A looking back pose turns the body away from the viewer while the head twists back over the shoulder to look toward them. The twist through the neck and spine creates a strong curve, and the glance makes it feel like a moment caught mid-movement.

sections.h: Why the looking back pose is so expressive
body: The pose combines a back view, which shows hair and the back of the costume, with a face, which carries the emotion. It suggests a story: the character was leaving and turned at the last moment. In Chinese culture the glance back, huimou (回眸), is a classic image in poetry and is often used with flowing traditional clothing.
It suits long hair and garments with movement: hanfu, kimono, capes, long skirts and ribbons, which swing with the turn.

sections.h: How to draw a looking back pose
body: Plan the twist in three parts: the hips point away, the ribcage turns partway, and the head turns the rest. No single joint can rotate the full 180 degrees, so the spine must spiral. Draw the shoulder line and hip line at different angles to show that rotation.

The near shoulder rises and comes forward, partly covering the chin; the neck shows a long diagonal muscle running from behind the ear to the front of the collarbone. Draw the face in 3/4 or profile, with the eyes turned farther toward the viewer than the head, which is what makes the glance read.

sections.h: How to pose and photograph a looking back
body: Have the subject stand with the back to the camera, weight on one leg, then turn the head over the shoulder nearest the light. Shoot from shoulder height; a slightly lower angle adds elegance to long outfits.

ul: Turn the shoulders a little toward the camera so the neck is not strained.
Drop the near shoulder so the chin can come over it.
Have the subject walk away and turn on a cue, and shoot a burst to catch hair and fabric in motion.
Keep the eyes on the lens or just past it; looking down reads shy, looking at the lens reads inviting.

faq.q: What is the looking back pose called?
faq.a: It is usually called the over-the-shoulder pose or looking back pose; in Chinese the glance is called huimou.

faq.q: Why does my looking back drawing look broken?
faq.a: The head is probably doing all the turning. Spread the twist through the hips, ribcage and neck so the spine spirals.

faq.q: How do I take a natural over-the-shoulder photo?
faq.a: Ask the subject to walk away and glance back on cue, and shoot a burst so you catch the moment hair and clothing swing.
